title: One Adam Update: Moments, Bias Correction, and the Parameter Step
purpose: Walk through a single scalar Adam timestep exactly as in Algorithm 1: form the first and second moment estimates from a toy prior state and the current gradient, apply bias correction, and compute the parameter update.
scope: One scalar parameter, one timestep t >= 1, with explicit toy prior moments m_prev and v_prev. No training loop, no model, no data pipeline. The gradient g is treated as given (a single observed gradient), not derived from a loss.
intuition: Adam keeps a running average of gradients (first moment) and of squared gradients (second moment). Because both averages start at zero, they are biased toward zero early on; dividing by 1 - beta^t removes that bias. The update then moves the parameter by the learning rate times the bias-corrected first moment divided by the square root of the bias-corrected second moment, so the step size is roughly controlled by the learning rate.
learning_objectives: Compute the first and second moment estimates and their bias-corrected versions for one scalar Adam step.
Compute the parameter update and explain how the learning rate and gradient magnitude set the step size.
prerequisites: Exponential moving averages: new = beta * old + (1 - beta) * current.
Basic algebra with square roots and powers, and the meaning of a learning rate.
assumptions: The gradient g is a single scalar observation at timestep t; no mini-batch or loss function is modeled.
The prior moments m_prev and v_prev are given toy values representing the state before this step.
limitations: Only one scalar parameter and one timestep are shown; multi-parameter behavior and long-run convergence are out of scope.
The gradient is supplied directly rather than computed from a loss, so no automatic differentiation or data is involved.
misconception: Bias correction is not an optional tweak: without dividing by 1 - beta1^t and 1 - beta2^t, the moments are systematically too small early in training and the step is distorted.
edge_cases: A zero gradient with zero prior moments gives zero moments and a zero update.
A very small second moment makes the denominator small, so the update can be large even for a modest gradient.

inputs.name: g
inputs.label: g
inputs.meaning: Current scalar gradient observation at this timestep.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.label: alpha
inputs.meaning: Learning rate (stepsize) multiplying the bias-corrected moment ratio.

inputs.name: beta1
inputs.label: beta1
inputs.meaning: Exponential decay rate for the first moment estimate.

inputs.name: beta2
inputs.label: beta2
inputs.meaning: Exponential decay rate for the second moment estimate.

inputs.name: epsilon
inputs.label: epsilon
inputs.meaning: Small constant added to the bias-corrected second moment inside the denominator for numerical stability.

inputs.name: t
inputs.label: t
inputs.meaning: Timestep index, a positive integer used in the bias-correction powers.

inputs.name: m_prev
inputs.label: m_prev
inputs.meaning: Toy first moment estimate carried into this step (state before the update).

inputs.name: v_prev
inputs.label: v_prev
inputs.meaning: Toy second moment estimate carried into this step (state before the update).

steps.name: m_t
steps.label: m_t
steps.meaning: First moment estimate: exponential moving average of the gradient.

steps.name: v_t
steps.label: v_t
steps.meaning: Second moment estimate: exponential moving average of the squared gradient.

steps.name: m_hat
steps.label: m_hat
steps.meaning: Bias-corrected first moment: divide by 1 - beta1^t to remove the zero-initialization bias.

steps.name: v_hat
steps.label: v_hat
steps.meaning: Bias-corrected second moment: divide by 1 - beta2^t.

steps.name: update
steps.label: update
steps.meaning: Parameter update: learning rate times bias-corrected first moment divided by the square root of the bias-corrected second moment plus epsilon.

explorations.title: Effect of gradient magnitude
explorations.observe: With a larger gradient, m_t, v_t, m_hat, v_hat and the update all change; the update scales roughly with the gradient direction while the denominator grows with its magnitude.
explorations.why: The first moment is linear in g, while the second moment is quadratic in g, so the ratio m_hat / sqrt(v_hat) reflects the signal-to-noise balance rather than the raw gradient size.

explorations.title: Effect of learning rate
explorations.observe: Changing alpha leaves the moment estimates and their bias corrections unchanged but scales the final update proportionally.
explorations.why: The learning rate multiplies the bias-corrected moment ratio, so it sets the overall step size without altering the moment statistics.
